findings.title: 68 GB Stolen From a Philippine Government Agency's Overseas-Employment Databases, Exposed by the Operator's Own Open Directory
findings.summary_md: Hunt.io reported that an unknown operator copied 68.837 GiB of 27 SQL Server backup files matching Philippine Overseas Employment Administration and migrant-worker systems in 23 minutes 46 seconds on 6 September 2026. The operator left the working folder open on a staging server at 213.163.205.35 (UpCloud, Singapore) on port 80, serving 543 requests from 76 addresses over 16 hours. The directory contained a rebranded GodPotato privilege escalation tool, a PowerShell stager, two payloads, and a full Impacket environment.

findings.title: Cybersecurity firm reports 68 GB of data from PH gov't agency found publicly online
findings.summary_md: Rappler summarized the Hunt.io finding, noting 27 SQL Server backups totaling 68.837 GB were copied on 6 September 2026. The National Privacy Commission is investigating; Philippine authorities are probing the suspected theft. Rappler emphasized that Hunt.io did not examine the contents of the backups, so the exact nature of potentially stolen files remains unconfirmed, though filenames point to migrant-worker administration systems.
